outcome: No known Wieferich prime in base 47 has been found or ruled in/out since 26 January 2024; no new base-47-specific search, bound, or theoretical result was located.
summary: The question is whether any base-47 Wieferich prime exists (a prime p, not dividing 47, with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p²). This is a pure existence question, and per §3.1 it can only be advanced by an actual resolution, not by a search extended further with no result. I confirmed via the current Wikipedia articles on 'Wieferich prime' and 'Wieferich pair', OEIS's 'Wieferich primes' wiki page, and general search that no base-47 Wieferich prime is known — the base-47 case appears only as the dead-end term in the Wieferich sequence starting from 3 (3, 11, 71, 47, ?), where no successor prime is known, a fact unchanged since well before 2024. I found no arXiv preprint, PrimeGrid project page, OEIS sequence update, or blog post reporting any computational search specifically extending the base-47 bound, and no theoretical work resolving the existence question for this base. Two tangentially related 2024-2026 arXiv papers turned up (on Wieferich primes for Drinfeld modules/function fields, and on number-field analogues tied to the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture) but both are generalizations to entirely different algebraic settings (function fields, number fields) rather than results about classical integer Wieferich primes in base 47, so per §3.1 they are related problems, not cases of this one, and do not change this bullet. No AI system was mentioned in connection with any base-47 Wieferich search. I therefore record no_change_found and status open, consistent with the triage's 'none' verdict, which I confirm rather than dispute.
competing_reading: None found. The two adjacent arXiv papers (Drinfeld-module and number-field Wieferich generalizations) could in principle be stretched to bear on 'base 47' if one reads 'base' extremely loosely as any algebraic base, but neither paper mentions base 47 or the rational-integer case at all, so this reading is not defensible.
what_would_settle_it: A computational search report (e.g., a PrimeGrid subproject page, an OEIS sequence update, or a preprint) stating a base-47 Wieferich prime found below some bound, or extending the known search-exhaustion limit for base 47 specifically, or a theoretical nonexistence/existence proof for this base.
